question: Which of the five has been most explicit about serving mass-affluent clients, and what exactly have they said?

cells.label: different_quantity

items.text: Schwab CEO Wurster stated that 61% of affluent clients ages 25 to 44 prefer to consolidate their wealth and banking relationships, and that households with $1 million to $5 million in assets using only one financial services firm jumped 11 percentage points year-over-year to 22%.
items.quote: The bull market for convenience is driving investors to increasingly consolidate their financial lives. 61% of affluent clients ages 25 to 44, so they prefer to consolidate their wealth and banking relationships. Households with $1 million to $5 million in assets using only one financial services firm jumped 11 percentage points year-over-year to 22%

items.text: Schwab Investor Day materials note that 68% of affluent investors want and are willing to pay for advice.
items.quote: 68% of affluent investors want & are willing to pay for advice 3

items.text: Schwab Advisor Services head Jon Beatty stated in a keynote that 68% of affluent Americans say they're willing to pay for advice today, up from 38% in 2010.
items.quote: Beatty noted that 68% of affluent Americans say they're willing to pay for advice today, up from 38% in 2010. "That is the market opportunity," he added.
items.unit: affluent Americans willing to pay for advice

items.text: Schwab President and CEO Rick Wurster said the firm is deepening relationships with higher net worth clients by continuing to strengthen its alternatives offer.
items.quote: We're also deepening relationships with our higher net worth clients by continuing to strengthen our alternatives offer.

items.text: Schwab stated it has some 3,000 financial advisors in-house, many holding CFPs, and that Wurster said the 400 branches serve Schwab retail clients seeking advice (not competing with RIAs for new wealth business).
items.quote: Schwab noted that it has some 3,000 financial advisors in-house, many of whom hold CFPs... Wurster said that the 400 branches Schwab had in 20 cities were to serve Schwab retail clients seeking advice

cells.differs_because: The sub-question asks what is new or most recent in Schwab's statements about mass-affluent clients specifically, but the passages state figures/statements about 'affluent' clients, 'affluent Americans'/'investors', or 'higher net worth' clients rather than a 'mass-affluent' segment as such; these are related wealth-tier statements, not the firm defining a mass-affluent segment.
cells.reason: Schwab's statements reference 'affluent' and 'higher net worth' clients (and Schwab Wealth Advisory), but no passage defines or addresses 'mass-affluent' clients specifically; these are related, adjacent wealth-segment statements.
